column1:
Cautiously optimistic with measured tightening, now tempered by Beige Book storm impacts and mild credit headwinds.

- FOMC stance: Labor market solid and growth moderate; inflation below 2% with a symmetric target; policy on hold while balance sheet normalization begins—gradualism and accommodative bias remain.
- Beige Book cross-check (August 2017): Reports modest to moderate growth overall but highlights hurricane-related disruptions. Dallas and Atlanta Districts noted impacts; Gulf Coast energy and natural resources (including the Eagle Ford) saw temporary shutdowns and disruptions to oil and natural gas production; agricultural conditions were mixed. These factors point to near-term softness and temporary energy-driven price pressures, consistent with the FOMC’s view that storms won’t materially alter the medium-term outlook.
- SLOOS cross-check: Banks reported weaker demand in several credit segments (CRE, construction/land development/multifamily; consumer auto and credit cards), with demand roughly unchanged for some nonfarm nonresidential loans. Standards eased for residential mortgages (including jumbo/QM/GSE) but tightened for consumer loans. Foreign banks tightened standards across C&I and CRE, even as some saw stronger CRE demand.

Implication: Labor strength and ongoing accommodation keep the outlook slightly positive, but Beige Book storm disruptions and SLOOS credit headwinds warrant a bit more caution near term.
